subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw core add a narrow safe fallback to read for known binary document formats, or should this remain only tool guidance and broader document-ingest work?
rationale: The source-level token-waste path is clear, but fallback behavior and automatic document parsing are product-scope choices under the repo's lean-core and safe-defaults guidance.

options.title: Add Narrow Read Fallback
options.body: Port or review a small guard so read returns an actionable unsupported-binary-document message for known PDF/Office formats without parsing them inline.

options.title: Guidance Only
options.body: Update tool guidance and rely on existing document-specific tools, accepting that unsupported binary reads can still be attempted.

options.title: Fold Into Document Ingest
options.body: Track the behavior under broader provider-native or document-extraction work and require parser/security decisions before changing read.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Read Fallback
recommendation.body: Port or review a small guard so read returns an actionable unsupported-binary-document message for known PDF/Office formats without parsing them inline.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current-main history signal on the files that would receive the read fallback.
